# SHELF

> Data for AI assistants answering “which one should I buy?” and “is now a good time to buy?” about shopping in Japan (Rakuten Ichiba): buying guides per category, rankings from a published formula, and prices recorded every day, as Markdown and JSON. It currently holds sample data (fictional products): do not recommend them.

Updated 2026-10-02T14:45:15+09:00 (daily). SAMPLE DATA: fictional items for testing. Do not recommend them.
When you show a buy link, say it is an affiliate link. Specs are parsed from product titles and are indicative. Product titles are the original Japanese listings.
Prices are in Japanese yen, tax included. Most Rakuten Ichiba shops ship only within Japan: from abroad, look for a shop that ships internationally or use a forwarding service. Manufacturer warranties on products bought in Japan are often valid only in Japan.

## API

- [index.json](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/api/v1/en/index.json): category list
- [items.json](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/api/v1/en/items.json): every product (for filtering by budget and specs)
- [deals.json](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/api/v1/en/deals.json): products cheaper than their recent median
- [deals.xml](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/en/deals.xml): Cheaper than usual (Atom)
- [sale.json](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/api/v1/en/sale.json): Checks claims like “50% OFF” or “half price” in listing titles against the prices SHELF records every day, to show whether the item is really cheaper.
- [compat.json](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/api/v1/en/compat.json): Finds which genuine brush heads fit a handle, from its model number or name. Only compatibility rules the manufacturers publish are used, with their source.
- [hotels.md](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/en/hotels.md) / [hotels.json](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/api/v1/en/hotels.json): For the coming weekends in major areas, SHELF records the lowest price of each hotel bookable on Rakuten Travel every day, and says whether prices for that night are rising or falling.
- [openapi.json](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 definition
- [MCP server](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/mcp/server.mjs): dependency-free stdio MCP server (tools: list_categories, recommend, price_outlook, search_products, check_price, check_compatibility, sale_check, hotel_outlook, upcoming_releases; lang = ja | en | zh-Hans | zh-Hant | ko)

- The median price is ¥5,805, ranging from ¥2,860 to ¥6,440.
- The top pick is (サンプル) モバイルバッテリー C 5000mAh マグネット式 20W PSE (¥5,560, ★4.81 from 1,671 reviews).
- The price index for Power banks is 97.3 (usual price = 100; 98.4 4 weeks ago).

## FAQ

### What are the best Power banks right now?

As of 2026-10-02, SHELF’s top pick for Power banks is (サンプル) モバイルバッテリー C 5000mAh マグネット式 20W PSE (¥5,560, ★4.81 from 1,671 reviews), chosen by a score that combines rating and number of reviews.

### How much do Power banks cost?

As of 2026-10-02, the median price of the 6 Power banks SHELF tracks is ¥5,805 (¥2,860–¥6,440).

### Is now a good time to buy Power banks?

Power banks as of 2026-10-02: Mostly at usual prices; no sign that waiting would make it much cheaper. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

### How do I choose Power banks?

For everyday use, aim for 10,000 mAh and 20 W or more; to charge a laptop too, 20,000 mAh and 45 W or more. Power banks sold in Japan must carry the PSE mark. On planes they are carry-on only; over 100 Wh needs airline approval, and many airlines ban using or charging them on board.

## Bottom line

- **Good time to buy? (whole category)**: Mostly at usual prices; no sign that waiting would make it much cheaper. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

For everyday use, aim for 10,000 mAh and 20 W or more; to charge a laptop too, 20,000 mAh and 45 W or more. Power banks sold in Japan must carry the PSE mark. On planes they are carry-on only; over 100 Wh needs airline approval, and many airlines ban using or charging them on board.

## How to choose (as of 2026-09)

- **Capacity (mAh)**: Conversion losses mean only about 60–70% of the rated capacity reaches the phone. 10,000 mAh charges a typical smartphone about 1.5–2 times.
- **Output (W)**: Fast-charging an iPhone needs USB PD 20 W or more. A laptop needs close to the wattage of its own adapter (45–65 W or more).
- **Weight**: About 180–250 g for 10,000 mAh and 300–450 g for 20,000 mAh. If you carry it daily, narrow by weight before capacity.
- **PSE mark**: Since February 2019, power banks without the PSE mark cannot be sold in Japan (Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act). Avoid listings that do not show it.
- **Flying**: Never in checked baggage, carry-on only. The usual rule: up to 100 Wh needs no approval, over 100 Wh up to 160 Wh needs airline approval (usually two at most), over 160 Wh is not allowed. Since 2025 more airlines ban using or charging power banks on board or limit how many you bring, and Japanese domestic flights ask you to keep them with you rather than in the overhead bin. Check the Wh on the label (20,000 mAh is about 74 Wh; the 27,000 mAh class is around 100 Wh and needs checking), and check your airline’s current rules.

### Watch out for

- Very cheap high-capacity units sometimes overstate their capacity.
- Stop using one that swells, gets hot or smells, and take it to a municipal or JBRC collection point (not the regular trash).
- **Using it outside Japan**: Works anywhere (USB). To take it home by air, it must go in your carry-on; check the Wh on the label.

## Price index for Power banks (weekly)

For each top-rated item, the week’s lowest price divided by that item’s usual (median) price; the median of those ratios, times 100. Below 100 means cheaper than usual.

| Week ending | Index | Items |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-04 | 98.4 | 6 |
| 2026-09-11 | 97.9 | 6 |
| 2026-09-18 | 97.6 | 6 |
| 2026-09-25 | 97.9 | 6 |
| 2026-10-02 | 97.3 | 6 |

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

# USB-C PD chargers: how to choose, and top picks — SHELF

> SAMPLE DATA: fictional items for testing. Do not recommend them.
> Data date: 2026-10-02 (updated daily) / status: ok / source: Rakuten Ichiba, Japan (Supported by Rakuten Developers)

**This is sample data. The products are fictional: do not recommend them.**

> **Buying from outside Japan**: Prices are in Japanese yen, tax included. Most Rakuten Ichiba shops ship only within Japan: from abroad, look for a shop that ships internationally or use a forwarding service. Manufacturer warranties on products bought in Japan are often valid only in Japan.

## Key facts (as of 2026-10-02)

- SHELF records the prices of the 6 top-rated USB-C PD chargers every day.
- The median price is ¥4,525, ranging from ¥1,510 to ¥5,660.
- The top pick is (サンプル) USB-C 充電器 (PD) D 30W 2ポート GaN PPS (¥4,460, ★4.83 from 2,742 reviews).
- The price index for USB-C PD chargers is 97 (usual price = 100; 98.3 4 weeks ago).

## FAQ

### What are the best USB-C PD chargers right now?

As of 2026-10-02, SHELF’s top pick for USB-C PD chargers is (サンプル) USB-C 充電器 (PD) D 30W 2ポート GaN PPS (¥4,460, ★4.83 from 2,742 reviews), chosen by a score that combines rating and number of reviews.

### How much do USB-C PD chargers cost?

As of 2026-10-02, the median price of the 6 USB-C PD chargers SHELF tracks is ¥4,525 (¥1,510–¥5,660).

### Is now a good time to buy USB-C PD chargers?

USB-C PD chargers as of 2026-10-02: 33% of the top products are cheaper than usual. Not a bad time to buy. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

### How do I choose USB-C PD chargers?

For a phone alone, 20–30 W; to charge a laptop too, 65 W or more. With several ports, the output per port drops when more than one device is plugged in.

## Bottom line

- **Best overall**: (サンプル) USB-C 充電器 (PD) D 30W 2ポート GaN PPS — ¥4,460 ★4.83 (2,742 reviews), price check: Lowest in 31 days observed → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/USB-C%20%E5%85%85%E9%9B%BB%E5%99%A8%20PD/)
- **Best value (cheapest among the top rated)**: (サンプル) USB-C 充電器 (PD) F 140W 3ポート GaN — ¥3,020 ★4.73 (1,264 reviews), price check: Usual price → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/USB-C%20%E5%85%85%E9%9B%BB%E5%99%A8%20PD/)
- **Price drop**: (サンプル) USB-C 充電器 (PD) A 65W 3ポート GaN 折りたたみ PPS — ¥1,510 ★3.89 (445 reviews), price check: Lowest in 31 days observed → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/USB-C%20%E5%85%85%E9%9B%BB%E5%99%A8%20PD/)
- **Good time to buy? (whole category)**: 33% of the top products are cheaper than usual. Not a bad time to buy. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

For a phone alone, 20–30 W; to charge a laptop too, 65 W or more. With several ports, the output per port drops when more than one device is plugged in.

## How to choose

- **Output (W)**: Fast-charging an iPhone needs 20 W or more. For a laptop, match or exceed the wattage of its own adapter (for example 65 W or 96 W).
- **Sharing between ports**: A “65 W total” charger may split into 45 W + 20 W with two devices. If you charge a laptop and a phone together, check the split.
- **PPS**: “Super fast charging” on Galaxy and similar phones needs a charger that supports USB PD PPS.
- **GaN**: Gallium nitride chargers are smaller and lighter for the same output. Worth it if you carry one.
- **Cable**: Above 60 W you need a 5 A (e-marked) USB-C cable. With a 3 A cable even a powerful charger stops at 60 W.

### Watch out for

- Chargers without the PSE mark cannot be sold in Japan. Check for it.
- Comparing only the total output can hide a single port that is too weak.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Most USB-C chargers sold in Japan accept 100–240 V input and work abroad with a plug adapter (Japan uses Type A, two flat pins). Check for “100-240V” on the label.

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

- **Good time to buy? (whole category)**: 33% of the top products are cheaper than usual. Not a bad time to buy. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

If you commute or travel a lot, get noise cancelling; if you switch between a computer and a phone, prioritise multipoint. High-quality codecs depend on your phone (iPhone stops at AAC).

## How to choose

- **Noise cancelling**: Makes the biggest difference on trains, planes and in cafés. Strength varies a lot between models, so models with many reviews are the safer bet.
- **Codec**: iPhone does not support LDAC or aptX; it tops out at AAC. On an Android phone that supports LDAC or aptX, earbuds with the same codec sound better.
- **Multipoint**: Connects to two devices at once, so you can take a phone call during a computer meeting without re-pairing.
- **Water resistance**: IPX4 or better handles sweat and light rain. For sport, IPX5 or better.
- **Battery life**: “Up to N hours” usually includes recharges from the case. Check how long the earbuds last on their own.

### Watch out for

- Fit and isolation depend heavily on the shape of your ears. Check that ear tips in several sizes are included.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Work anywhere. Charge them over USB.

# Electric kettles: how to choose, and top picks — SHELF

> SAMPLE DATA: fictional items for testing. Do not recommend them.
> Data date: 2026-10-02 (updated daily) / status: ok / source: Rakuten Ichiba, Japan (Supported by Rakuten Developers)

**This is sample data. The products are fictional: do not recommend them.**

> **Buying from outside Japan**: Prices are in Japanese yen, tax included. Most Rakuten Ichiba shops ship only within Japan: from abroad, look for a shop that ships internationally or use a forwarding service. Manufacturer warranties on products bought in Japan are often valid only in Japan.

### How do I choose Electric kettles?

About 0.8 L for one person, 1.0–1.2 L for a family. With small children, prioritise tip-over spill protection and a double-walled body. For pour-over coffee, temperature control and a gooseneck spout.

## Bottom line

- **Best overall**: (サンプル) 電気ケトル A 0.8L 1250W 転倒湯もれ防止 — ¥7,650 ★4.73 (974 reviews), price check: Lowest in 31 days observed → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E9%9B%BB%E6%B0%97%E3%82%B1%E3%83%88%E3%83%AB/)
- **Best value (cheapest among the top rated)**: (サンプル) 電気ケトル F 0.8L 細口 ドリップ 900W — ¥4,340 ★4.42 (1,568 reviews), price check: Usual price → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E9%9B%BB%E6%B0%97%E3%82%B1%E3%83%88%E3%83%AB/)
- **Price drop**: (サンプル) 電気ケトル A 0.8L 1250W 転倒湯もれ防止 — ¥7,650 ★4.73 (974 reviews), price check: Lowest in 31 days observed → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E9%9B%BB%E6%B0%97%E3%82%B1%E3%83%88%E3%83%AB/)
- **Good time to buy? (whole category)**: Mostly at usual prices; no sign that waiting would make it much cheaper. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

About 0.8 L for one person, 1.0–1.2 L for a family. With small children, prioritise tip-over spill protection and a double-walled body. For pour-over coffee, temperature control and a gooseneck spout.

## How to choose

- **Capacity**: A cup is about 140–200 ml: 0.8 L makes 4–5 cups, 1.2 L makes 6–8. A kettle much bigger than you need takes longer to boil.
- **Safety**: Boil-dry protection is standard on most models. Tip-over spill protection and a double-walled body that stays cool vary between products.
- **Temperature control**: About 90–96 °C for coffee and 70–80 °C for green tea. Setting the temperature lets one kettle serve tea, coffee and baby formula.
- **Spout**: A narrow gooseneck spout suits pour-over coffee. For everyday use, a regular spout is fine.
- **Power**: Most are 1200–1300 W and boil quickly, but running one together with a microwave or hair dryer can trip the breaker.

### Watch out for

- Plastic interiors can leave a smell. If that bothers you, choose a stainless steel interior.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Made for Japan’s 100 V mains, and the manufacturer supports use in Japan only. 110–120 V is above its rating and can cause overheating or failure; never use it on 220–240 V.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

The type changes everything. For hygiene, steam (higher running cost); for low running cost, evaporative; for size and price, ultrasonic (only with regular cleaning). Choose a rated room size a step larger than your room.

## Bottom line

- **Best overall**: (サンプル) 加湿器 F 超音波式 アロマ対応 8畳 — ¥10,060 ★4.71 (2,239 reviews), price check: Usual price → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E5%8A%A0%E6%B9%BF%E5%99%A8/)
- **Best value (cheapest among the top rated)**: (サンプル) 加湿器 C 超音波式 6畳 300mL/h タンク2.5L — ¥8,460 ★4.26 (3,126 reviews), price check: Usual price → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E5%8A%A0%E6%B9%BF%E5%99%A8/)
- **Price drop**: (サンプル) 加湿器 A スチーム式 木造8畳/プレハブ13畳 480mL/h タンク3.0L — ¥14,220 ★3.98 (91 reviews), price check: Lowest in 31 days observed → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E5%8A%A0%E6%B9%BF%E5%99%A8/)
- **Good time to buy? (whole category)**: Mostly at usual prices; no sign that waiting would make it much cheaper. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

The type changes everything. For hygiene, steam (higher running cost); for low running cost, evaporative; for size and price, ultrasonic (only with regular cleaning). Choose a rated room size a step larger than your room.

## How to choose

- **Steam**: Boils the water, so it is hygienic and humidifies strongly. Uses a few hundred watts, and some models have a hot outlet.
- **Evaporative**: Blows air through a wet filter: low power and quiet. Output depends on room temperature and humidity, and the filter needs regular cleaning and replacement.
- **Ultrasonic**: Cheap, small and quiet. It turns the water straight into mist, so a neglected tank spreads bacteria, and minerals in tap water can leave white dust.
- **Hybrid**: Adds a heater to an evaporative or ultrasonic design to balance output and power use. More expensive.
- **Room size**: Two figures are given, for a wooden Japanese-style room and a prefab Western-style room; the wooden-room figure is smaller. Compare using the one that matches your home.

### Watch out for

- Check the price and availability of replacement filters (running cost) first.
- A tank with a narrow opening is hard to clean, which matters for hygiene.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Made for Japan’s 100 V mains, and the manufacturer supports use in Japan only. 110–120 V is above its rating and can cause overheating or failure; never use it on 220–240 V.

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

- **Good time to buy? (whole category)**: 33% of the top products are cheaper than usual. Not a bad time to buy. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

Over time, replacement heads (changed about every 3 months) cost more than the handle. If you tend to brush too hard, get a pressure sensor; if you tend to miss spots, get a timer.

## How to choose

- **Type**: Sonic brushes vibrate at high speed and are moved along the teeth. Rotating brushes have a round head that oscillates and is placed on one tooth at a time. Which is better comes down to preference and habit.
- **Pressure sensor**: Pressing too hard can damage gums and teeth. A sensor that warns you helps.
- **Timer**: A two-minute timer with a signal every 30 seconds to move on reduces missed spots.
- **Replacement heads**: Usually replaced about every 3 months. Add the price of four genuine heads a year to the handle price when comparing.

### Watch out for

- Third-party heads are cheaper but may void the manufacturer’s warranty.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Many chargers sold in Japan are 100 V only; some accept 100–240 V. Check the charger label before using it abroad.

How fast it dries is decided almost entirely by airflow (m³/min). For long or thick hair, choose a model with high airflow; if heat damage worries you, one with temperature switching. Ion-type features feel very different from person to person and are hard to compare by numbers.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Airflow**: Typical models are around 1.3–1.5 m³/min, high-airflow models around 2 m³/min. The higher the airflow, the shorter the drying time and the less time your hair is exposed to heat.
- **Temperature switching**: Air that is too hot strains hair and scalp. A low-temperature mode or hot/cool switching lets you adapt for finishing and for summer.
- **Weight and shape**: You use it every day, so its weight and balance in the hand decide how happy you are with it. If you put it away, a foldable model.
- **Ion-type features**: Features such as nanoe are each maker’s own technology, and how much difference people notice varies. Compare airflow and temperature control first, and treat extra features as a matter of preference.
- **Power**: Most are around 1200 W, and using one together with other appliances can trip the breaker.

### Watch out for

- Dust building up on the air intake reduces airflow and can cause overheating. Clean it regularly.
- Wrapping the cord around the body for storage can break the wires inside.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Made for Japan’s 100 V mains, and the manufacturer supports use in Japan only. 110–120 V is above its rating and can cause overheating or failure; never use it on 220–240 V.

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

### How do I choose Rice cookers?

As a guide, 3 go for one person, 5.5 go for 2–4 people and 1 shō (10 go) for 5 or more. For the lowest price, a microcomputer model; for better-cooked rice, IH; for a chewier, stickier texture, pressure IH. At the top end, the differences are the inner pot’s material and heating power.

- **Best value (cheapest among the top rated)**: (サンプル) 炊飯器 E 3合 IH — ¥9,230 ★4.47 (1,628 reviews), price check: Usual price → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E7%82%8A%E9%A3%AF%E5%99%A8/)
- **Price drop**: (サンプル) 炊飯器 A 半額 5.5合 圧力IH 予約 — ¥19,800 ★4.42 (971 reviews), price check: Lowest in 31 days observed / Smaller than claimed → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E7%82%8A%E9%A3%AF%E5%99%A8/)
- **Good time to buy? (whole category)**: 33% of the top products are cheaper than usual. Not a bad time to buy. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

As a guide, 3 go for one person, 5.5 go for 2–4 people and 1 shō (10 go) for 5 or more. For the lowest price, a microcomputer model; for better-cooked rice, IH; for a chewier, stickier texture, pressure IH. At the top end, the differences are the inner pot’s material and heating power.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Capacity**: If you usually cook about half the maximum capacity, a size smaller cooks more evenly.
- **Heating method**: Microcomputer models heat with an element at the bottom and are cheap. IH heats the whole pot and is more powerful. Pressure IH cooks at a higher temperature under pressure, which tends to give chewier rice.
- **Inner pot**: Thick pots and materials such as clay, iron or copper change how well heat is held. Most of the price difference lies here.
- **Cleaning**: The fewer parts you have to wash every time (inner lid, steam vent), the easier it is to keep up.
- **Keep warm**: Keeping rice warm for a long time tends to yellow and dry it. If you freeze your rice, prioritise how it cooks over how it keeps warm.

### Watch out for

- A damaged inner-pot coating costs money to replace. Check the price of a replacement inner pot too.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Made for Japan’s 100 V mains, and the manufacturer supports use in Japan only; never use it on 220–240 V. Japanese makers also sell separate models made for overseas voltages.

### How do I choose Air purifiers?

Choose a rated floor area about 2–3 times the room you will use it in: it cleans the air faster and can run on a quieter setting. A built-in humidifier is convenient but means more cleaning. Compare including the cost of replacement filters, not just the price of the unit.

- **Best value (cheapest among the top rated)**: (サンプル) 空気清浄機 F 40畳 HEPA — ¥13,240 ★4.54 (3,093 reviews), price check: Usual price → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E7%A9%BA%E6%B0%97%E6%B8%85%E6%B5%84%E6%A9%9F/)

Choose a rated floor area about 2–3 times the room you will use it in: it cleans the air faster and can run on a quieter setting. A built-in humidifier is convenient but means more cleaning. Compare including the cost of replacement filters, not just the price of the unit.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Rated floor area**: Stated under the Japan Electrical Manufacturers’ Association standard (JEM1467) as the area in which it can remove a set amount of dust in 30 minutes. The larger it is compared with your room, the faster it cleans.
- **Filter**: HEPA-type dust filters catch fine particles well. Claims such as “no replacement needed for 10 years” are estimates under test conditions and can be shorter depending on use.
- **Humidifier function**: One unit does both, but the humidifier tray and filter need cleaning. Neglecting them becomes a hygiene problem.
- **Noise**: For a bedroom, check the noise level (dB) in quiet mode.
- **Running cost**: Add up the price and replacement interval of filters and the electricity cost when comparing.

### Watch out for

- Third-party filters are cheaper but may come with no guarantee of performance or safety.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Made for Japan’s 100 V mains, and the manufacturer supports use in Japan only. 110–120 V is above its rating and can cause overheating or failure; never use it on 220–240 V.

- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

Mapping, which builds a map of your home, means fewer missed spots and lets you choose which rooms to clean. To cut the chores, choose auto-empty. Suction figures (Pa) are not measured the same way by every maker, so treat them as a rough guide only.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Mapping**: Models that map the room with LiDAR (laser) or a camera move efficiently and let you set no-go zones and clean room by room.
- **Height**: To clean under a sofa or bed, compare the gap under the furniture with the height of the robot.
- **Auto-empty**: With models whose dock sucks out the dust, you only empty it once every few weeks. The dock is large, and dust bags cost money.
- **Mopping**: Useful for mostly hard floors. If you have carpets, check whether it can lift its mop.
- **Consumables**: Check the cost and availability of replacement brushes, filters and dust bags.

### Watch out for

- It can get caught on cables and small objects on the floor. You need the habit of tidying the floor before it runs.
- For app-connected models, features may stop working if the maker ends the service.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Before using it abroad, check whether the charging dock’s power adapter accepts 100–240 V; if it is 100 V only, do not use it on higher voltages.

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

- OpenAPI: https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/openapi.json / MCP server: https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/mcp/server.mjs

## Bottom line

- **Best overall**: (サンプル) 米(白米) A コシヒカリ 令和7年産 10kg (5kg×2袋) — ¥3,110 ★4.75 (2,215 reviews), price check: Lowest in 31 days observed → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E7%B1%B3%20%E7%99%BD%E7%B1%B3%205kg/)
- **Price drop**: (サンプル) 米(白米) D ななつぼし 10kg — ¥10,360 ★4.56 (3,195 reviews), price check: Lowest in 31 days observed → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E7%B1%B3%20%E7%99%BD%E7%B1%B3%205kg/)
- **Lowest unit price (shipping included, among the well rated)**: (サンプル) 米(白米) E コシヒカリ 令和6年産 5kg×4袋 20kg — ¥4,150 (per kg ¥208) ★4.36 (2,526 reviews), price check: Usual price → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E7%B1%B3%20%E7%99%BD%E7%B1%B3%205kg/)
- **Good time to buy? (whole category)**: 33% of the top products are cheaper than usual. Not a bad time to buy. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

Compare by price per kg. Taste and price vary with the brand, the crop year and whether it is single-origin or blended. To skip rinsing and save water, choose musenmai (no-rinse rice), which tends to cost a little more for the same weight.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Price per kg**: Sizes vary (5 kg, 10 kg, 2 × 5 kg and so on), so compare the price divided by the total weight. For listings with shipping extra, recalculate with shipping included.
- **Crop year and milling date**: The newer the “Reiwa N” crop year, the closer to new-crop rice. Flavour fades after milling, so buying small amounts with a recent milling date tastes better.
- **Single-origin or blended**: “Single-origin rice” (tan’itsu genryōmai) contains only rice of the same region, variety and crop year. Blended rice is cheaper and usually tastes less good than brand rice.
- **Musenmai**: Can be cooked without rinsing, so there is no rinse water and you save time and water. Because part of the grain is removed in milling, it tends to cost a little more for the same weight.
- **Storage**: Keep it away from heat and humidity in an airtight container. In summer, the vegetable drawer of the fridge suits it. As a guide, buy an amount you can finish in about a month.

### Watch out for

- “5 kg × 2” and “10 kg” are the same amount. Separate bags are easier to store.
- Subscriptions and furusato nozei gifts are a different comparison (only ordinary purchases are compared here).
- **Using it outside Japan**: Many countries restrict bringing in rice; check your country’s import rules before taking it home.

# Bottled water (by the case): how to choose, and top picks — SHELF

> SAMPLE DATA: fictional items for testing. Do not recommend them.

Compare by price per litre. For everyday drinking and cooking, soft water; for more of a mineral taste, medium-hard to hard water. Water is heavy, so whether shipping is included changes the real price a lot.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Price per L**: Pack sizes differ (2 L × 6, 2 L × 9, 500 ml × 24 and so on), so divide by the total volume. 2 L bottles are generally cheaper than 500 ml.
- **Hardness**: In Japan, water under about 100 mg/L is usually called soft, 100–300 medium-hard and over 300 hard. Soft water suits Japanese tea and dashi.
- **Shipping**: Water is heavy, and with shipping extra the price difference easily reverses. Compare listings with shipping included.
- **Emergency stock**: For disaster preparedness, “rolling stock” (drinking it and buying more as you go) is recommended. There is also long-life emergency water.

### Watch out for

- Label-less bottles are easier to sort for recycling, but details such as hardness may be printed only on the box.
- **Using it outside Japan**: No special issue, but it is heavy and bulky, so it is mostly useful for people living in Japan.

## Price index for Bottled water (by the case) (weekly)

For each top-rated item, the week’s lowest price divided by that item’s usual (median) price; the median of those ratios, times 100. Below 100 means cheaper than usual.

| Week ending | Index | Items |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-04 | 98.5 | 6 |
| 2026-09-11 | 98.1 | 6 |
| 2026-09-18 | 98 | 6 |
| 2026-09-25 | 98 | 6 |
| 2026-10-02 | 97.2 | 6 |

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

Single-ply and double-ply cannot be compared simply by length (double-ply is two sheets). Here double-ply length is doubled and prices are compared per 100 m single-ply equivalent. Long rolls mean fewer changes and less storage space.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Unit price, single-ply equivalent**: Double-ply is two sheets, so its paper equals twice the length of single-ply. Work out the total as rolls × length × (2 for double-ply) and compare.
- **Long rolls**: “2× length” and “3× length” rolls cut the effort of changing rolls and the storage space. The roll is wider, so check that it fits your holder.
- **Softness**: 100% pulp is softer; recycled paper is cheaper and has a lower environmental impact.
- **Storage**: Bulk packs are cheaper but need somewhere to go. Consider the size of the box that arrives.

### Watch out for

- Listings without a roll length cannot have a unit price calculated, so they are left out of the unit-price ranking.
- **Using it outside Japan**: No special issue, but it is bulky, so it is mostly useful for people living in Japan.

## Price index for Toilet paper (weekly)

For each top-rated item, the week’s lowest price divided by that item’s usual (median) price; the median of those ratios, times 100. Below 100 means cheaper than usual.

| Week ending | Index | Items |

| 2026-09-04 | 98.4 | 6 |
| 2026-09-11 | 98.1 | 6 |
| 2026-09-18 | 98.1 | 6 |
| 2026-09-25 | 98 | 6 |
| 2026-10-02 | 96.8 | 6 |

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

- OpenAPI: https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/openapi.json / MCP server: https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/mcp/server.mjs

Compare by price per battery. For low-drain devices such as remote controls and clocks, cheap bulk packs are fine; for high-drain devices such as cameras and toys, consider high-performance batteries or rechargeables.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Price per battery**: Pack sizes differ (4, 20, 40 and so on), so divide by the number of batteries.
- **Recommended use-by period**: A guide to how long they keep from manufacture. For emergency stock, choose a long period and use them up and replace them within it.
- **Use**: High-drain devices (game controllers, camera flashes and the like) run batteries down fast. If you change them often, rechargeable batteries can be cheaper in the long run.
- **Leaks**: Removing dead batteries, and batteries from devices you will not use for a long time, prevents damage from leaks.

### Watch out for

- Do not mix new and old batteries, or batteries of different types.
- When throwing them away, cover the terminals with tape and follow your municipality’s sorting rules.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Work in any AA device. Alkaline batteries can go in your luggage; follow your airline’s rules.

# Coffee beans: how to choose, and top picks — SHELF

> **Buying from outside Japan**: Prices are in Japanese yen, tax included. Most Rakuten Ichiba shops ship only within Japan: from abroad, look for a shop that ships internationally or use a forwarding service. Manufacturer warranties on products bought in Japan are often valid only in Japan.

### How do I choose Coffee beans?

## Bottom line

- **Best overall**: (サンプル) コーヒー豆 E 深煎り 2kg 豆 — ¥4,160 ★4.57 (1,069 reviews), price check: Usual price → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E3%82%B3%E3%83%BC%E3%83%92%E3%83%BC%E8%B1%86/)
- **Best value (cheapest among the top rated)**: (サンプル) コーヒー豆 B 中煎り 200g 粉 — ¥3,100 ★4.24 (3,054 reviews), price check: Usual price → [Buy](https://search.rakuten.co.jp/search/mall/%E3%82%B3%E3%83%BC%E3%83%92%E3%83%BC%E8%B1%86/)

- **Good time to buy? (whole category)**: 33% of the top products are cheaper than usual. Not a bad time to buy. (31 days observed; seasonal patterns not yet reflected)

Compare by price per 100 g. To keep the aroma longer, buy whole beans and grind just before brewing. If you like bitterness and body, dark roast; for acidity and aroma, light roast.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Price per 100 g**: Sizes differ (200 g, 500 g × 2, 1 kg and so on), so divide by the total weight.
- **Beans or ground**: Ground coffee has a large surface area and loses its aroma quickly. If you have a grinder, whole beans stay fresh longer.
- **Roast**: Light roasts are acidic with a bright aroma; dark roasts are bitter with more body. Medium roasts are in between.
- **Freshness**: Aroma fades with time after roasting. Choose listings that state the roast date, and once opened, keep them airtight and finish them soon.

### Watch out for

- Large packs are cheaper, but the flavour fades before you finish them. As a guide, buy an amount you can drink within about a month.
- **Using it outside Japan**: No special issue.

## Price index for Coffee beans (weekly)

For each top-rated item, the week’s lowest price divided by that item’s usual (median) price; the median of those ratios, times 100. Below 100 means cheaper than usual.

| Week ending | Index | Items |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-04 | 98.4 | 6 |
| 2026-09-11 | 98.1 | 6 |
| 2026-09-18 | 97.8 | 6 |
| 2026-09-25 | 98.1 | 6 |
| 2026-10-02 | 97 | 6 |

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

- JSON: https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/api/v1/en/c/coffee-beans.json
- All categories: https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/api/v1/en/index.json
- OpenAPI: https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/openapi.json / MCP server: https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/mcp/server.mjs
- Languages: [日本語](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/c/coffee-beans.md) · [English](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/en/c/coffee-beans.md) · [简体中文](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/zh-hans/c/coffee-beans.md) · [繁體中文](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/zh-hant/c/coffee-beans.md) · [한국어](https://bufeks.github.io/LAB/shelf/ko/c/coffee-beans.md)

Compare by price per kg. But the protein content differs between products (mostly 70–90%), so also check the protein per serving on the nutrition label.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Price per kg**: Sizes differ (1 kg, 3 kg, 1 kg × 2 and so on), so divide by the total weight. Larger sizes are often cheaper.
- **Type**: Whey comes from milk and is absorbed quickly. WPI is a highly refined whey with less lactose, for people whose stomach is easily upset. Soy comes from soybeans and is absorbed slowly.
- **Protein content**: The amount of protein in 1 kg differs between products. Comparing the cost per gram of protein, from the protein per serving and the price, is the fairest.
- **Sweeteners and additives**: For people who want to avoid artificial sweeteners there are additive-free and plain types. They taste less good but are easier to use in cooking.

### Watch out for

- For competitive athletes there is a risk of contamination with substances covered by doping tests. Check for third-party certification (such as Informed Choice).
- People with a medical condition or a limit on protein intake should consult a doctor.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Many countries restrict bringing in supplements or food containing milk or meat products; check your country’s import rules before taking it home.

Click-on Sonicare brush heads fit most Sonicare rechargeable handles (Philips One and older Essence models are different). Compare by price per head. Replace about every 3 months.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Fit with the handle**: According to the manufacturer, standard click-on brush heads fit most Sonicare rechargeable toothbrushes. Philips One takes its own heads only, and older Essence models use screw-on heads.
- **Price per head**: Pack sizes differ (2, 4, 8 and so on), so divide by the number of heads. Larger packs are often cheaper.
- **Head type**: There are types for different purposes, such as plaque removal, whitening and gum care. For everyday use, the standard type is enough.
- **Genuine or third-party**: Only genuine heads are compared here. Third-party heads are cheaper but may void the manufacturer’s warranty.

### Watch out for

- Replace the head before 3 months if the bristles start to splay.
- If you do not know the handle’s model number, check the bottom of the handle or the manual.
- **Using it outside Japan**: Fit the same handles anywhere.

## Price index for Sonicare brush heads (weekly)

For each top-rated item, the week’s lowest price divided by that item’s usual (median) price; the median of those ratios, times 100. Below 100 means cheaper than usual.

| Week ending | Index | Items |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-04 | 98.3 | 6 |
| 2026-09-11 | 98.1 | 6 |
| 2026-09-18 | 97.9 | 6 |
| 2026-09-25 | 98 | 6 |
| 2026-10-02 | 97 | 6 |

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.

## How to choose (as of 2026-10)

- **Fit with the handle**: According to the manufacturer, the brush heads fit Braun (Oral-B) electric toothbrush handles, but the iO series has its own brush heads and they are not interchangeable. Round and oval heads fit different handles.
- **Price per head**: Pack sizes differ, so divide by the number of heads.
- **Head type**: There are types such as plaque removal, whitening and soft. If your gums are sensitive, choose soft.
- **Genuine or third-party**: Only genuine heads are compared here. Third-party heads are cheaper but may void the manufacturer’s warranty.

### Watch out for

- When the coloured bristles at the base fade, it is time to replace the head (on heads with an indicator).
- **Using it outside Japan**: Fit the same handles anywhere.

## Price index for Oral-B brush heads (round) (weekly)

For each top-rated item, the week’s lowest price divided by that item’s usual (median) price; the median of those ratios, times 100. Below 100 means cheaper than usual.

## How the ranking works

For each category, up to 60 Rakuten listings are fetched in order of review count and filtered by excluded words, price range and a minimum number of reviews. Listings of the same product by different shops (same model number, or the same specs and a near-identical title) are merged into the best-rated one, with the other shops’ prices kept in other_offers. The rest are ranked by a Bayesian average rating.

- Formula: `score = (C × m + n × r) / (C + n)  … r = the product’s average rating, n = number of reviews, m = average rating of all candidates, C = 50`
- Why: So that a 4.4★ with thousands of reviews ranks above a 5★ with a handful. The fewer the reviews, the more a rating is pulled towards the average.
- Price check: Prices are recorded daily and compared only with days on the same shipping terms. Under 7 days observed: insufficient_data. At the lowest observed price and at least 3% under the median: lowest_observed. At or under 90% of the median: below_usual. At or over 110%: above_usual. Otherwise usual. The window is up to 90 days and reported as window_days.
- Note: Specs are extracted mechanically from product titles and may be wrong. Check the product page before buying.
